newsitem.title: USA: PAN official expects Mexico elections will be fair.
newsitem.headline: PAN official expects Mexico elections will be fair.

text.p: Vicente Fox, governor of Mexico's Guanajuato state and an official of the National Action Party (PAN), said he expects a level playing field in the July 6 midterm elections.

"There's no choice," Fox said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "For the first time, the opportunity is right there for the opposition to have a majority in Congress and also to gain some more of the governorships."
Long the main opposition to the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), the PAN now trails the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) in the race for mayor of Mexico City.

Fox said the likelihood of PRD candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas being elected Mexico City mayor did not diminish the PAN's possible victories in Congress. The entire lower house and a fourth of the Senate are up for election.
"There is no real power in the Mexico (City) governorship," Fox said. "It is really important to (focus) on Congress."
Asked how the conservative PAN would interact with the other parties, Fox said he expected some cooperation.

"It will be a most interesting triangle," he said. "This new Congress will force the (deputies) to look for cohesiveness on decision-making. I envision many times you will see the PAN together with the PRI pushing very strongly on the economic front."

The PAN has worked regionally, particularly in Guanajuato state, to extend social benefits to more of the population, Fox said. He said the party was seeking to provide better access to education, banking and credit.
